**Abstract.** In this paper, we review the representation theory of the inﬁnite symmetric group, and we extend the works of Kerov and Vershik by proving that the irreducible characters ofS∞ always satisfy a central limit theorem. Hence, for any point of the Thoma simplex, the corresponding measures on the levels Yn of the Young graph have a property of gaussian concentration. By using the Robinson-Schensted-Knuth algorithm and the theory of Pitman operators, we relate these results to the properties of certain random per- mutations obtained by riﬄe shuﬄes, and to the behaviour of random walks conditioned to stay in a Weyl chamber.
